working_definition: T3 is a columnar T-type optic lobe neuron with its soma adjacent to the medulla--lobula plate gap. Its cell body fiber bifurcates in the second optic chiasm to form one bushy arborization in medulla layer M9 and a second arborization in lobula layers 2 and 3. It is capable of both glutamatergic and GABAergic neurotransmission and is present in a single copy per optic column (unicolumnar).

best_match.fbbt_definition: T neuron with its soma posteriorly adjacent to the gap between the medulla and lobula plate and a cell body fiber that projects along the proximal surface of the medulla before branching in the second optic chiasm (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). One branch forms a bushy, fine, terminal arborization in medulla layer M9 and the other forms a terminal arborization in lobula layers 2 and 3 with mix of bleb-type and fine terminal branches (Morante and Desplan, 2008; Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989). It seems to be capable of both glutamatergic and GABAergic neurotransmission.

The dual glutamatergic/GABAergic neurotransmitter capacity cited in the FBbt definition (Raghu and Borst, 2011; Raghu et al., 2013) matches the cluster's known transmitter profile.
